scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You put in just five hundred rupees, and suddenly you own a slice of fifty companies. How does a mutual fund do that?

scenes.name: pool
scenes.text: A mutual fund collects money from thousands of people into one big pool.

scenes.name: manager
scenes.text: A fund manager invests that pool in shares, bonds or both, according to the fund's stated goal.

scenes.name: units
scenes.text: In return you get units. Your share of the fund depends on how many units you hold.

scenes.name: nav
scenes.text: Every day the fund's value is divided by its units. That price per unit is called the NAV.

scenes.name: sip
scenes.text: With a SIP, you invest a fixed amount every month, buying more units when prices are low.

scenes.name: risk
scenes.text: Funds charge a small yearly fee called the expense ratio, and returns are not guaranteed. Markets go up and down.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Pool, invest, track the NAV. Growing together. Follow for more on how things really work.
